item.title: nixos/fprintd: Add separate enablePam option to fprintd service
item.description:
Because fprintd does not have a mechanism to ensure user attention, using it to authenticate to programs such as sudo or su is not secure. This was assigned CVE-2024-37408. A comment was added to the PAM fprintAuth option to make this clear.

This commit also adds the option services.fprintd.enablePam, which is now used to control the default use of the fprintd PAM authorization. Enabling this option emits an evaluation-time warning so users are aware of this issue. This setting defaults to services.fprintd.enable for now, but could default to false in future releases.

See #442117 for more details, discussion can continue there for better mitigation. Perhaps in the future enablePam could accept an option such as "attention", which would only enable it for PAM services that opt-in.

Backward incompatible changes:

 The security fixes above harden the SUID mount(8) against TOCTOU
 attacks.  As a side effect, the following features are restricted
 for non-root users:

 X-mount.subdir=
   Restricted to Linux >= 6.15 for non-root users.  The old-kernel
   implementation uses namespace unsharing and string-based
   move_mount() which is unsafe (TOCTOU).  The safe detached subdir
   open is available only on Linux >= 6.15.

 X-mount.nocanonicalize
   Ignored for non-root users.  Paths must always be canonicalized
   in restricted mode to ensure safe target resolution before
   fd pinning.

item.title: Add integration test for verifying that cryptsetup luksSuspend correctly wipes the volume key from memory
item.description:
A couple days ago I made the scary observation that, starting with Linux kernel 6.9, more specifically commit a28d893eb3270cf62c10dd8777af0d8452cdc072, cryptsetup luksSuspend silently fails in wiping the volume key from memory.

This command (or its library version in libcryptsetup) is for instance used by systemd-homed and cryptsetup-suspend to safely lock an encrypted volume on laptop suspend.

(NB: cryptsetup-suspend is a Debian package, but I guess that several NixOS folks privately have a version of it, as it scratches a common itch. I intend to offer my own clone as a separate pull request soon.)

This pull request adds a test verifying whether cryptsetup luksSuspend succeeds. On current kernels, it fails. If you want to experience the test passing, add boot.kernelPackages = pkgs.linuxKernel.packages.linux_6_6. I'm working with upstream to get this resolved.
